description: Blame Attribution Tab — a deep-dive view within the Run Recap page that shows which iteration's code changes caused each verification failure. When the agentic verification loop fails to converge, users need to understand causality: not just which checks failed, but which specific iteration introduced the regression. The blame engine (a deterministic, file-path-based algorithm — no LLM calls) cross-references error output (stdout/stderr from verification steps) against per-iteration git diffs to attribute failures to specific iterations. This tab surfaces blame attributions, oscillation warnings (same file modified 3+ consecutive iterations), revert patterns (change-undo-change cycles), and escalation status. Data comes from the MCP endpoint GET /task-runs/{id}/blame which parses iteration_results.blame_json from the task run's result_data. Real-time updates arrive via the AppEvent::BlameAttribution Tauri event during active runs.

groups.name: Page Identity and Navigation
groups.description: The Blame Attribution tab lives within the Run Recap page's tabbed interface, alongside Timeline, Verification, Knowledge, Context, Canvas, and Errors tabs. Users reach it by clicking the tab after a workflow run completes (or during a run, for live blame data). The tab should clearly communicate its purpose: explaining WHY failures happened, complementing the Verification tab which shows WHAT failed.

assertions.description: The Blame tab appears in the Run Recap tab bar so users can navigate to blame attribution data alongside other analysis views
assertions.precondition: User has navigated to the Run Recap page for a completed or in-progress workflow run

assertions.description: Clicking the Blame tab switches the content area to display blame attribution data, following the same tab-switching pattern used by the existing Verification and Knowledge tabs

groups.name: Blame Summary Statistics
groups.description: At the top of the Blame tab, aggregate statistics give users an at-a-glance understanding of how many failures were attributed, how many files are oscillating, and how many revert patterns were detected. These numbers come from the GET /task-runs/{id}/blame response fields: total_attributions, total_oscillating_files, total_revert_patterns. Users use these to gauge the severity of convergence problems before diving into per-iteration details.

assertions.description: Users can see the total number of verification failures that were attributed to specific iterations, giving them an immediate sense of how many failures have known causes
assertions.precondition: At least one iteration had verification failures with blame data (blame_json is non-null in at least one IterationResult)

assertions.description: Users can see how many files are exhibiting oscillation (modified in 3+ consecutive iterations), which is a strong signal that the AI is stuck in a loop on those files
assertions.precondition: The run had 3+ iterations where the same file was modified consecutively

assertions.description: Users can see how many files exhibit revert patterns (change-skip-change cycles with 2+ gaps), indicating the AI's fixes are being undone across iterations
assertions.precondition: The run had files modified in a non-consecutive alternating pattern across 3+ iterations

assertions.description: Users can see how many iterations produced blame data, contextualizing the attribution count against the total iteration count
assertions.precondition: At least one iteration had verification failures

groups.name: Per-Iteration Blame Detail
groups.description: The core of the Blame tab: a chronological list of iterations that produced blame data. Each iteration section shows which verification steps failed and which previous iteration's changes caused each failure. The data comes from the blame_reports array in the GET /task-runs/{id}/blame response. Each report contains attributions (step name, blamed iteration, implicated files with line ranges, confidence score, explanation). Users read this to understand the causal chain: 'Iteration 3's TypeScript check failed because iteration 2 modified Card.tsx.'

assertions.description: Each iteration with blame data has a clearly labeled header showing the iteration number, so users can correlate blame data with the iteration timeline in other tabs
assertions.precondition: At least one iteration produced blame attributions

assertions.description: Each attribution shows the name of the verification step that failed, matching the step names shown in the Verification tab for cross-referencing
assertions.precondition: At least one verification step was blamed

assertions.description: Each attribution prominently shows which iteration introduced the breaking change, so users know exactly when the regression was introduced
assertions.precondition: At least one verification step was blamed

assertions.description: Each attribution displays a confidence level (High >= 0.8, Medium >= 0.5, Low < 0.5) indicating how certain the blame engine is about the attribution. High confidence means multiple files from the error output matched a single iteration's diff. Low confidence means no file paths were extractable and the most recent iteration was blamed by default.
assertions.precondition: At least one verification step was blamed

assertions.description: Each attribution lists the specific files that were implicated — files mentioned in the verification error output that were also modified in the blamed iteration's diff. File paths are shown with their iteration of modification.
assertions.precondition: At least one attribution has implicated_changes with file paths

assertions.description: Each attribution includes a human-readable explanation of why the blame was assigned, such as 'File Card.tsx explicitly referenced in error output was modified in iteration 2'
assertions.precondition: At least one verification step was blamed

groups.name: File Oscillation Warnings
groups.description: When the blame engine detects that a file has been modified in 3 or more consecutive iterations, it surfaces an oscillation warning. This is a strong signal that the AI is stuck: it keeps changing the same file but the fix never sticks. The UI should make these warnings visually prominent (they represent the most actionable finding in the blame data). The oscillating_files array in each BlameReport contains the file path, the number of consecutive iterations (consecutive_blames), and the specific iteration numbers involved.

assertions.description: When oscillation is detected, a visually distinct warning section appears, drawing the user's attention to files that the AI is repeatedly failing to fix
assertions.precondition: total_oscillating_files > 0 in the blame response

assertions.description: Each oscillating file shows its path so the user can identify which specific file is being thrashed
assertions.precondition: At least one file has been modified in 3+ consecutive iterations

assertions.description: Each oscillating file shows how many consecutive iterations it was modified in, indicating severity (3 is concerning, 5+ is a definitive stuck loop)
assertions.precondition: At least one file has been modified in 3+ consecutive iterations

assertions.description: When no files exhibit oscillation, the oscillation warning section is not shown, avoiding unnecessary noise when the loop is making progress normally
assertions.precondition: total_oscillating_files == 0 in the blame response

groups.name: Revert Pattern Warnings
groups.description: Revert patterns are detected when a file is modified in a non-consecutive alternating pattern (present, absent, present) across iterations with at least 2 gaps. This indicates the AI's changes are being undone — possibly by other fixes that conflict, or by the AI itself reverting its previous approach. These are shown separately from oscillation warnings because the behavior pattern (intermittent vs consecutive) and the recommended response differ. Revert patterns are excluded for files already flagged as oscillating to avoid duplicate warnings.

assertions.description: When revert patterns are detected, a warning section appears showing which files exhibit change-revert-change cycles
assertions.precondition: total_revert_patterns > 0 in the blame response

assertions.description: Each revert pattern entry shows the file path and the specific iterations where it was modified, so users can trace the change-revert cycle in the git history
assertions.precondition: At least one file exhibits a revert pattern

groups.name: Empty and Loading States
groups.description: The Blame tab must gracefully handle cases where no blame data exists — either because the run completed on the first iteration (no failures to attribute), the run is still in its initial verification phase, or blame analysis produced no attributions (all failures had generic error messages with no extractable file paths).

assertions.description: When the run passed verification on the first iteration (no failures), the Blame tab shows an informative empty state explaining that blame attribution is only generated when verification fails
assertions.precondition: The run completed successfully on the first verification iteration with no failures

assertions.description: While blame data is being fetched from the GET /task-runs/{id}/blame endpoint, a loading indicator is shown rather than a blank content area
assertions.precondition: The blame data fetch is in progress

groups.name: Live Blame Updates During Active Runs
groups.description: During an active run, blame data is emitted in real-time via the AppEvent::BlameAttribution Tauri event (event name: 'blame-attribution'). The event payload includes task_run_id, iteration, attributed_failures count, oscillating_files count, revert_patterns count, and the full blame_json. The tab should update incrementally as new iterations complete, without requiring a manual page refresh. This allows users to observe blame accumulation in real-time and intervene early if they see oscillation forming.

assertions.description: When a new blame-attribution event arrives for the current task run, the Blame tab appends the new iteration's blame data without discarding previously displayed iterations
assertions.precondition: The user is viewing the Blame tab for an actively running workflow that has emitted at least one blame-attribution event

assertions.description: Summary statistics (total attributions, oscillating files, revert patterns) update in real-time as new blame events arrive, reflecting the cumulative state
assertions.precondition: Multiple blame-attribution events have been received during the current viewing session

groups.name: Escalation Policy Status
groups.description: The escalation policy (EscalationPolicy struct on LoopConfig) controls warnings and 'rethink' prompts when the loop fails to make progress. warn_after (default: 3) triggers a warning log. rethink_after (default: 5) injects a meta-prompt telling the AI to step back and reconsider its approach — it fires at the threshold, then every 3 iterations after. time_limit_secs enforces a wall-clock deadline checked in CheckPreconditions. The Blame tab should surface escalation events so users understand when and why the system intervened.

assertions.description: When the escalation policy's warn_after threshold has been crossed, the user can see that a warning was emitted, indicating the loop is struggling to make progress
assertions.precondition: verification_failures >= warn_after threshold (default: 3)

assertions.description: When the rethink_after threshold is crossed, the user can see that a 'rethink' meta-prompt was injected into the AI's failure context, asking it to take a fundamentally different approach
assertions.precondition: verification_failures >= rethink_after threshold (default: 5) and (failures - threshold) % 3 == 0

assertions.description: When the escalation policy's time_limit_secs was exceeded, the user can see that the loop was stopped due to a wall-clock time limit, with the elapsed time displayed
assertions.precondition: The run was terminated by escalation_time_limit (CompletionReason::PhaseTimeout with phase 'escalation_time_limit')

groups.name: Cross-Tab Referencing
groups.description: The Blame tab's value is amplified when users can cross-reference blame data with other Run Recap tabs. Iteration numbers in blame attributions should correlate with the Timeline tab. Failed step names should match entries in the Verification tab. File paths in implicated changes can be correlated with the git diff context shown in the Context tab. This cross-referencing is architectural — it does not require explicit navigation links, but the naming and numbering must be consistent across tabs.

assertions.description: Iteration numbers shown in blame attributions use the same numbering scheme as the Timeline and Verification tabs (1-indexed, matching LoopContext.iteration)
assertions.precondition: At least one blame attribution exists and the Timeline/Verification tabs are also populated
assertions.expected: Iteration numbers match across Blame, Timeline, and Verification tabs for the same run

assertions.description: Failed step names in blame attributions (e.g., 'TypeScript compilation', 'CSS layout check') exactly match the step names shown in the Verification tab, since both come from VerificationPhaseResult.step_results[].step_name
assertions.precondition: At least one blame attribution exists
assertions.expected: Step names are identical to those in the Verification tab

groups.name: Cross-Run Learning Integration
groups.description: Blame attributions are recorded as causal events in SQLite via record_blame_as_causal_events() — each attribution becomes a causal edge with cause_type 'iteration_change' and effect_type 'verification_failure', relationship 'caused_by_change'. Oscillation patterns are stored as cause_type 'file_oscillation' / effect_type 'convergence_stuck'. The cross_run_learning.rs module queries these events to detect systemic patterns across runs (e.g., the same file is blamed across multiple independent runs). This is a backend-only integration but the Blame tab should document it for architectural awareness.

assertions.description: When the same file has been blamed across multiple previous runs (detected via cross-run learning causal events), the Blame tab indicates this is a recurring issue rather than a one-off, helping users prioritize root-cause investigation
assertions.precondition: The cross_run_learning system has detected that the same file was blamed in 2+ previous runs
assertions.notes: This assertion documents a future capability. The causal events are stored but the cross-run query for 'same file blamed repeatedly' is not yet surfaced in the UI.

states.name: Loading — Fetching Blame Data
states.description: Blame data is being fetched from the GET /task-runs/{id}/blame endpoint. A loading indicator (progressbar) is visible. No blame content, summary statistics, or warning sections are shown.

transitions.name: No blame data available (run passed first iteration or no attributions)

states.name: Empty — No Blame Attributions
states.description: The run passed verification on the first iteration or blame analysis produced no attributions. An informative empty-state message explains that blame attribution is only generated when verification fails. No summary statistics, iteration details, or warning sections are shown.

transitions.name: User navigates to a different run, triggering a reload
A blame-attribution event arrives for an active run that previously had no blame data

states.name: Blame Populated — Attributions and Summary Visible
states.description: Blame data has loaded successfully. The summary statistics section shows total attributions, oscillating files count, and revert patterns count. Per-iteration blame detail sections are visible with iteration headers, failed step names, blamed iteration references, confidence levels, implicated files, and explanation text. Oscillation and revert warning sections appear conditionally based on the data. Escalation status indicators may be present if thresholds were crossed.

transitions.name: User navigates to a different run, triggering a reload
A new blame-attribution Tauri event arrives, indicating the run is still active

states.name: Live Updating — Receiving Real-Time Blame Events
states.description: The run is actively in progress and blame-attribution Tauri events are arriving. The summary statistics update incrementally as new iterations complete. New iteration blame sections are appended without discarding previously displayed ones. Oscillation and revert warnings may appear or update as patterns emerge across iterations. A live-update indicator distinguishes this state from the static blame-populated state.

transitions.name: Run completes and no further blame events will arrive
User navigates to a different run

states.name: Error — Failed to Load Blame Data
states.description: The GET /task-runs/{id}/blame request failed. An error message is displayed explaining the failure. No blame content, summary statistics, or warning sections are shown.

transitions.name: User retries or navigates to a different run

metadata.author: Claude Opus 4.6
apiEndpoints: MCP: GET /task-runs/{id}/blame -> { task_run_id, task_name, total_iterations_with_blame, total_attributions, total_oscillating_files, total_revert_patterns, blame_reports: [{ iteration, report: BlameReport }] }
Tauri Event: blame-attribution -> { task_run_id, iteration, attributed_failures, oscillating_files, revert_patterns, blame_json }
Tauri Event: iteration-metrics (existing, for convergence context)
SQLite: causal_events table (write-only from blame engine, read by cross_run_learning)
